chat_panel.welcome_auto:
Hi! 👋 I'm **Tessbrain** — your company's digital brain.

I'll figure out the best way to answer — quickly find a fact or run a deep analysis.

**What I can do:**
- 📊 Status of projects, tasks and decisions
- 👥 Information about employees and teams
- 📝 Agreements and meeting outcomes
- ⚠️ Risks, issues and anomalies
- 💡 Analytics and recommendations

**Just ask** — I'll handle it!
chat_panel.welcome_instant:
⚡ **Instant mode** — answers with no wait.

Ready summaries from the knowledge base in a fraction of a second. No waiting — just facts.

**Best for:**
- "Show me a summary of project Alpha"
- "Tell me about Ivanov"
- "What projects are active right now?"

⏱️ Less than 1 second
chat_panel.welcome_quick:
🔍 **Quick mode** — fast search.

I'll find information in the knowledge base and give a short answer.

**Best for:**
- "When did we last discuss the budget?"
- "Who's responsible for marketing?"
- "What tasks were assigned at the last meeting?"

⏱️ 3–5 seconds
chat_panel.welcome_standard:
📊 **Standard mode** — full analysis.

Search across the whole knowledge base, analysis of relationships, detailed answer.

**Best for:**
- "What issues exist in this project and who owns them?"
- "Compare the progress of two teams"
- "What product decisions did we make last month?"

⏱️ 8–15 seconds
chat_panel.welcome_deep:
🧠 **Deep mode** — in-depth research.

Multi-step analysis: search, hypothesis checking, contradiction detection, audit and recommendations.

**Best for:**
- "What can we optimize in our company?"
- "What hidden risks are in current projects?"
- "Audit: where are we losing efficiency?"
- "Why is project X delayed?"

⏱️ 30 seconds — 2 minutes
chat_panel.welcome_tasker:
📋 **Tasker mode** — quick spec generation.

Describe the task — I'll create a technical specification based on company data.

**Examples:**
- "Create a spec for our product's landing page"
- "Prepare a launch plan for a new feature"
- "Draft a brief for the website redesign"

⏱️ 1–3 minutes
chat_panel.welcome_tz:
📄 **Spec mode** — detailed technical specification.

Deep analysis: I'll find all task data, analyze meetings and documents, identify gaps and create a **professional spec** with source citations.

**For which tasks:**
- 🔌 APIs and integrations
- 🎨 Landings and marketing
- 💰 Financial models
- ⚙️ New features
- 🏗️ System architecture
- 📈 Reports and analytics

💡 Select meetings or documents on the left — the spec will be more accurate.

⏱️ 2–5 minutes
chat_panel.welcome_agentic:
🤝 **Agentic mode** — multi-agent analysis.

A team of AI agents works together: one plans, another searches, a third verifies, a fourth crafts the answer.

**Best for complex questions:**
- "Run a full analysis of our business"
- "Compare all projects: timelines, risks, resources"
- "What does the company do and what are the product advantages?"
chat_panel.welcome_mark:
Hi! 📈 I'm **Mark** — your marketing assistant.

I can help you:
- 🎯 Build a marketing strategy
- 📝 Write content and copy
- 🔍 Analyze competitors
- 💡 Generate promotion ideas

**Describe the task!** For example:
- "Analyze example.com"
- "Write copy for a landing page"
- "Create a content plan for a month"
chat_panel.welcome_automation:
Hi! ⚡ I'm **MeetFlow Automation** — task automation.

**Choose a mode above:**

✅ **Tasks** — YouGile, Trello, Jira, Telegram, Email
🌐 **Web** — AI controls the browser (any sites)
🎙️ **MeetFlow** — work with meetflow.synlabs.pro
📞 **Calls** — work with calls.synlabs.pro

**Examples:**
- "Create a task: Prepare presentation"
- "Go to the website and find information"
- "Send in Telegram: Reminder"
chat_panel.welcome_transcripts:
Hi! 🎙️ This is the **meetings & documents chat**.

I answer strictly from the materials you select — on a private model, in a **closed environment**, without sending data to external APIs.
Made for confidential meetings and documents.

**Select meetings, projects or documents on the left** and ask a question:
- "What did we agree on at the last meeting?"
- "Find risks in project X"
- "Summarize the salary discussion"
chat_panel.automation_tasks:
Hi! ✅ **Tasks** — an agent team for meetings and task trackers.

**What I can do:**
- 📅 Instantly list your MeetFlow meetings and tasks (no agents needed)
- 📋 Take a task from a meeting and create it in **YouGile / Trello / Jira**, update statuses
- 📨 Send summaries/tasks to **Telegram** or **Gmail**
- 🗓️ Create **Google Calendar** events and **Notion** pages

**Examples:**
- "List my recent meetings"
- "Show my tasks for the month"
- "Take tasks from the 'Board meeting' and create them in YouGile"

ℹ️ Trackers, Telegram and Gmail work when connected in Integrations.
chat_panel.automation_web:
Hi! 🌐 **Web** — AI drives a real browser (experimental).

**What I can do:** open sites, click, fill forms, extract data.

**Requires:** `pip install stagehand playwright && playwright install chromium`.

⚠️ Slow (real browser). For reading MeetFlow/Calls data use the neighbouring modes — much faster.
chat_panel.automation_meetflow:
Hi! 🎙️ **MeetFlow** — a conversation about your meetings.

**Just ask in plain words:**
- "Show my recent meetings"
- "What was the last meeting about?"
- "What did we decide on the team call?"
- "Find meetings for project X"

I answer from your meeting data (list, summaries, content) and remember the dialog — you can follow up.

ℹ️ For actions (create a task, send to Telegram) use the Tasks mode.
chat_panel.automation_calls:
Hi! 📞 **Calls** — calls.synlabs.pro integration (call analytics).

**What I can do:**
- 👤 Customer 360 card — just send a phone number
- 🎯 "Find customers for <your offer>" — AI search over call history with readiness scores
- 📊 "Daily report" (add "refresh" to rebuild)
- ⏱️ "How many minutes left" — plan usage
- 🗣️ Otherwise — Voice-of-Customer report from accumulated events

ℹ️ Needs a CallInsight key (CALLINSIGHT_API_KEY or MEETFLOW_API_KEY).
chat_panel.automation_tess:
Hi! 🧩 **Tess** — the fastest and cheapest executor.

Simple requests run on local FunctionGemma (free) or with no LLM at all; complex ones are finished by Gemini. Ollama not running? Everything still works via Gemini.

**What I can do:** tasks, meetings, decisions, people from the knowledge base; send to Telegram; create tasks; manage automations ("create / show mine / cancel").

**You control the tools:** the checkboxes below limit what I'm allowed to call.

💡 Free mode: `ollama pull functiongemma && ollama serve`.
chat_panel.automation_hybrid:
Hi! 🔀 **Fast Agent** — short auto-actions in 2–4 steps.

Find → process → deliver, fast. For long multi-step jobs use the Agent tab.

**Examples:**
- "Email me the summary of the last meeting"
- "Find marketing tasks and send them to Telegram"
- "Take a task from the last meeting and create it in YouGile"
- "In 2 hours send a call reminder" — creates a delayed automation
- "What automations do I have?" — lists them

**Integrations:** Telegram, Gmail, Jira, Trello, Notion, Slack, Sheets, HubSpot and more.
chat_panel.automation_openclaw:
Hi! 🐾 **OpenClaw** — agentic task execution mode.

The AI agent receives your task in **natural language** and **decides on its own** which tools to use, in what order, and synthesizes the result.

**Key differences:**
- 🧠 The agent **plans the chain** of actions itself
- 🔄 Full **execution trace** — every step is visible
- 🛠️ Access to **all** Tessbrain tools simultaneously
- 📝 Tasks described in **free text**

**Examples:**
- "Find the last meeting, extract tasks, and email them"
- "Check tasks in Trello and create a summary in Notion"
- "Find all meetings this week and send a digest to Telegram"
- "Analyze project decisions and create a report"

Just describe the task — the agent figures it out!
chat_panel.automation_agent_oc:
Hi! 🤖 **Agent** — the most capable mode for complex multi-step jobs.

Plans a chain of up to 30 steps on its own, sees the company knowledge graph and all tools, verifies the goal at the end, and **learns**: a successful run is saved as a skill and reused next time.

**Choose me when** the job has many stages across different sources.

**Examples:**
- "Collect all project decisions for the month, build a report and email it"
- "Check Trello tasks, find overdue ones and write a summary to Notion"

💬 Keep the dialog going: I remember session context ("now send that to TG").

sima_consultant_svc.no_io_data_suggestion: Open block → "What" tab → fill "Input data" and "Output data"
sima_consultant_svc.low_progress_desc: Block "{name}" contains little information. Fill at least the key sections.
sima_consultant_svc.low_progress_suggestion: Use "AI fill all sections" for quick filling
sima_consultant_svc.short_description_desc: Description of block "{name}" is under 30 chars. Expand for clarity.
sima_consultant_svc.short_description_suggestion: Add details: what exactly the module does, what tasks it solves
sima_consultant_svc.core_no_implementation_desc: Block "{name}" is the system core but has no implementation described. Critical for planning.
sima_consultant_svc.core_no_risks_desc: Core block "{name}" has no risk analysis.
sima_consultant_svc.isolated_block_desc: Block "{name}" is not connected to any other block. You may need to add connections, or it's an error.
sima_consultant_svc.isolated_block_suggestion: Drag a connection to/from this block on the canvas or ask AI to add connections
sima_consultant_svc.cycle_desc: There is a cyclic dependency in the schema. It might be intentional (feedback loop), but worth checking.
sima_consultant_svc.cycle_suggestion: Check "dependency" connections — one might need to be "data_flow"
sima_consultant_svc.high_fanout_desc: Block "{name}" has {count} outgoing connections. Consider decomposing into submodules.
sima_consultant_svc.high_fanout_suggestion: Consider creating a subschema for this block
sima_consultant_svc.no_core_desc: No "core" type blocks. A product typically has a core — the main module everything builds around.
sima_consultant_svc.no_core_suggestion: Identify the main module and change its type to "core"
sima_consultant_svc.no_data_desc: No "data" type blocks. Any product needs data storage.
sima_consultant_svc.no_data_suggestion: Add a block for the database, cache or file storage
sima_consultant_svc.same_type_title: All blocks of the same type
sima_consultant_svc.same_type_desc: All {count} blocks are type "{type}". Components should be separated by purpose.
sima_consultant_svc.same_type_suggestion: Split into core / data / integration / AI agents
sima_consultant_svc.conn_no_desc_desc: Connection between "{from}" and "{to}" is not described. Without description it's unclear what's passed.
sima_consultant_svc.conn_no_desc_suggestion: Click connection → fill description or click "AI describe"
sima_consultant_svc.conn_no_format_suggestion: Specify what's passed (dataDescription) and in what format (dataFormat)
sima_consultant_svc.conn_duplicate_desc: Between "{from}" and "{to}" there are {count} connections. Consider merging.
sima_consultant_svc.conn_duplicate_suggestion: Remove the duplicate or specify different connection types
sima_consultant_svc.no_mvp_desc: No block is marked as MVP. Define the minimal set of modules for launch.
sima_consultant_svc.no_mvp_suggestion: Pick 2-5 key blocks and set their layer to "mvp"
sima_consultant_svc.all_mvp_desc: All {count} blocks are marked as MVP. This likely means no prioritization.
sima_consultant_svc.all_mvp_suggestion: Split blocks: keep most important in MVP, move rest to "medium" or "ideal"
sima_consultant_svc.no_ideal_desc: No "ideal" layer blocks. Having a dream-product vision is useful for strategic planning.
sima_consultant_svc.no_ideal_suggestion: What features make the dream product? Add them as ideal blocks
sima_consultant_svc.few_modules_desc: Schema has only {count} block(s). Products usually consist of 5-15 modules.
sima_consultant_svc.few_modules_suggestion: Think what else: auth? API? Analytics? Notifications? Admin panel?
sima_consultant_svc.no_connections_desc: No connections at all. Modules should be connected to understand data flows.
sima_consultant_svc.no_connections_suggestion: Drag an arrow from one block to another on the canvas
sima_consultant_svc.few_connections_desc: {connections} connections for {blocks} blocks. Each block usually has at least one connection.
sima_consultant_svc.few_connections_suggestion: Check that all modules are connected to the rest of the system

banana_node_help.image_input_what: Image source: upload a file or paste from the clipboard (Ctrl+V).
banana_node_help.image_input_example: Product photo → Generation: "place it on a marble table".
banana_node_help.annotation_what: Markup on top of the image: arrows, frames, captions.
banana_node_help.annotation_connect: Input ← image. Output → "Generation" (takes the marks into account).
banana_node_help.annotation_example: Circle the sofa → "replace the circled area with a leather sofa".
banana_node_help.text_combiner_what: Combines several texts into one: a template with '{{'placeholders'}}'.
banana_node_help.nano_banana_what: Image generation (or video for Veo models).
banana_node_help.nano_banana_connect: Inputs ← a prompt (required) and up to 3 reference images. Output → "Result" or the next "Generation".
banana_node_help.nano_banana_example: Prompt "slide with a growth chart" + a style reference → slide.
banana_node_help.llm_generate_what: Text generation by a neural network (headlines, descriptions, scripts).
banana_node_help.llm_generate_example: "Write 5 headlines for a landing page about …" → a list.
banana_node_help.infographic_what: Dense meeting infographic: the image model draws the map, key facts are duplicated as text in the caption.
banana_node_help.infographic_connect: Input ← “Ask brain” / meeting text. Output → “Notify” (photo + facts to Telegram).
banana_node_help.infographic_example: Meeting summary → a “knowledge map” infographic with numbers and decisions → to Telegram.
banana_node_help.output_what: Final result: the finished image will appear here.
banana_node_help.output_connect: Input ← "Generation". Then you can download it.
banana_node_help.output_example: The last block of each branch.
banana_node_help.trigger_what: Process start: manually or on a schedule (every N minutes).
banana_node_help.trigger_connect: Output → the first step of the process ("Ask the brain", "Report"…).
banana_node_help.trigger_example: "Every 1440 min" → a weekly digest is compiled automatically.
banana_node_help.ask_brain_what: A question to the company knowledge base — the Tessbrain brain will answer.
banana_node_help.ask_brain_connect: Input ← trigger/previous step (the input text will be inserted). Output → "Condition", "Notify", "Task".
banana_node_help.ask_brain_example: "What decisions were made this week and by whom?"
banana_node_help.report_what: Generate a report using a methodology (summary, metrics…).
banana_node_help.report_example: Type "summary" → a weekly digest in Telegram.
banana_node_help.notify_what: Send a message to Telegram or by email.
banana_node_help.notify_connect: Input ← any step (its output becomes the text if the field is empty).
banana_node_help.notify_example: Brain answer → a notification to the manager.
banana_node_help.task_what: Create a task in the system from the previous step output.
banana_node_help.condition_what: A fork: if the input contains the text — the "yes" branch, otherwise "no".
banana_node_help.condition_connect: Input ← step. Two outputs: yes ↗ / no ↘.
banana_node_help.wait_reply_what: Sends a message to Telegram and waits for a person's reply. The process pauses until an answer arrives.
banana_node_help.wait_reply_connect: Input ← step (what to send). Output → the next step receives the person's reply text.
banana_node_help.wait_reply_example: Draft summary → editor "Any edits?" → wait for reply → mind-map to the client with the edits applied.
banana_node_help.meeting_data_what: Pulls specific data from a meeting: summary, tasks, decisions, participants, transcript, agenda or a ready-made report.
banana_node_help.meeting_data_connect: Input — not needed (or a meeting ID from a previous step). Output → report/map/Telegram. On a meeting trigger it uses that meeting automatically.
banana_node_help.meeting_data_example: Trigger "Meeting ended" → "Meeting data: tasks" → to the manager in Telegram.
banana_node_help.meeting_share_what: Creates a public meeting link via MeetFlow: an outside person opens it and works at the chosen access (view/edit/admin).
banana_node_help.meeting_share_connect: Input — not needed (or a meeting ID from a previous step). Output → the link flows into Notify/Telegram/email. On a meeting trigger it uses that meeting automatically.
banana_node_help.meeting_share_example: Meeting ended → "Share (view)" → link to the client in Telegram.
banana_node_help.document_what: Builds a business document (proposal/contract/card) with the real document module: type structure, company details, facts from input only.
banana_node_help.document_connect: Input ← meeting summary (+ CRM/web context). Output → Notify/email or PDF download.
banana_node_help.document_example: Meeting → summary + CRM data + web → "Document: proposal" → email to client.
banana_node_help.crm_data_what: Fetches data from CRM/dataset (client, current prices) as text context.
banana_node_help.crm_data_connect: Input — not needed (query on node) or a query from a previous step. Output → Document/Proposal as context.
banana_node_help.crm_data_example: "CRM data: concrete prices and client info" → into "Document: proposal".
banana_node_help.web_search_what: Searches the web (client site, market) and returns findings as text.
banana_node_help.web_search_connect: Input — not needed (query on node) or from a previous step. Output → Document/Proposal as context.
banana_node_help.report_xlsx_what: Builds a native Excel file (.xlsx) from previous steps' data: tables, line items, totals. Numbers stay numbers — Excel computes on them.
banana_node_help.report_xlsx_connect: Input ← a report/table/data (e.g. from CRM data, Report or Generate). Output → Notify sends the .xlsx as an attachment.
banana_node_help.report_xlsx_example: "CRM data: sales by month" → "Report → Excel" → email with .xlsx.
banana_node_help.translate_what: Translates text or a document from the previous step into the chosen language, keeping numbers, prices and names intact.
banana_node_help.translate_connect: Input ← any text/document. Output → Notify/email or another Document.
banana_node_help.translate_example: "Document: proposal" → "Translate: to English" → email to an overseas client.
banana_node_help.doc_edit_what: Edits a finished document by your command ("remove section", "make it shorter") and returns it in full, adding no new facts.
banana_node_help.doc_edit_connect: Input ← a document from the previous step. Output → Notify/email or Document to render as PDF.
banana_node_help.doc_edit_example: "Document: proposal" → "Edit: remove payment terms" → email to client.
banana_node_help.crm_write_what: Writes back to CRM: creates a deal/lead or adds a comment to a record ("CRM history updated"). Behind the ENABLE_CRM_WRITEBACK flag.
banana_node_help.crm_write_connect: Input ← text (used as the comment body). Output → Notify/next step (record ID and link).
banana_node_help.crm_write_example: Lead → "Document: proposal" → "Write to CRM: create deal" → comment "proposal sent".

chat_sources_card.title: Chats as a brain source
chat_sources_card.feature_disabled: The feature is turned off on the server (ENABLE_CHAT_INGEST). Sources are visible, but nothing is being collected.
chat_sources_card.telegram_hint: Telegram group: add the company bot to the group and type /brain_on there. The sender must be recognizable to the system: either their Telegram is listed in “Integrations → Telegram → Contacts”, or they are linked via the “Connect” button. The bot must have privacy mode turned off (/setprivacy with @BotFather), otherwise it does not see ordinary group messages. Nothing is stored before the command.
chat_sources_card.slack_hint: Slack: enter bot_token on the “Integrations → Slack” tab (scope channels:history) and list the channels below.
chat_sources_card.files_title: Whether to collect document attachments (pdf/docx/txt/md/csv) from this chat into the knowledge base. Turning it off does not delete files already collected. In “context only” mode files never go to the brain anyway.
chat_sources_card.mode_title: “To brain” — the digest goes into the knowledge base. “Context only” — never uploaded to the brain, available solely as an explicitly selected chat context (for chats with partners and the like)
chat_sources_card.participants_heading: Participants and linking to people from meetings (linking happens only with your confirmation):
chat_sources_card.analysis_heading: Extracted by analysis (every item is backed by a quote from the chat):
chat_sources_card.dropped_unverified: Dropped for lack of a verbatim quote: {count}
chat_sources_card.webhook_base_placeholder: Public https URL of the backend (tunnel/prod), e.g. https://brain.mycompany.com
chat_sources_card.import_hint: Telegram export: chat → ⋮ → Export chat history → JSON — paste the contents of result.json. WhatsApp: chat → More → Export chat (without media) — paste the text. This is exactly the way to go for WhatsApp: the API does not return group history, the export does.
chat_sources_card.import_title_placeholder: Title (optional — will be taken from the export)
chat_sources_card.import_text_placeholder: Paste result.json or the WhatsApp export text here
chat_sources_card.footer_note: “To brain” stores the raw messages as a KB document “Chat: …” — from there search and reports see them like any other document. No paraphrasing: what was written is what you get. Cloud API does not expose WhatsApp groups — that is on the roadmap.

model_settings_panel.heading: 🧠 Models
model_settings_panel.description: Which models think for you. If nothing is set, the platform models are used (Standard — fast, Premium — powerful, with a fallback on failures). Your own models apply everywhere: chats, search, sync, boards, automations, SIMA. A «🎫 Subscription» on Premium means research, complex reports and batch sync (1 call instead of 30 on a powerful model) go through your CLI login (Claude Pro / ChatGPT / Google) without an API key; concurrency is limited, and when the subscription limit is reached there is a silent fallback to the platform models. Interactive chat never uses the subscription.
